C-INDEX-METRIC.Summary: The citation index `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml` is budgeted by whole-file line count, but retirement flips an `Entry` `layer` attribute in place and never removes a line, and the persisted ceiling is clamped so it can only hold or fall — so the index base only rises and no shipped operation returns capacity. Its live headroom is one entry (measured 2026-09-09 at `3ba0d77a76ba108be5a60e740d83dc2b734a7c46`: `base="340" headroom="1" ceiling="341"`). The maintainer has chartered the remedy, V1 + M1: the index budget is measured by live `Entry` count — direct children of the root whose `layer` attribute is not `"retired"`, mirroring the rule `registry.xml` already applies to rows — and the index root's `base` / `headroom` / `ceiling` are rewritten once, in this bundle's own diff, to the new unit. No new tool mode is added. The genre-aware breach diagnostic ships in this bundle and is not deferred. Two remedies were considered and rejected by the charter and stay rejected here: giving the index a retired sibling (the index is the citation directory of every token, live or retired, and `layer` is precisely the pointer saying where the body now lives), and re-deriving the ceiling from the current base (that is exactly a number that can be raised to pass). Derived at this commit and agreed with the charter: the rewritten root carries `base="256" headroom="40" ceiling="296"` — base is the live `Entry` count (338 direct `Entry` children, 82 with `layer="retired"`), headroom is the shipped index headroom constant 40, and ceiling is what the shipped `persistSnapshot` clamp yields: `min(341, 256 + 40) = 296`. This bundle implements [RM-GOVERNED-PATH](../../../../docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/plan.md) record integrity; it pays the staged finding F205 (the index ratchet), which is cited as staged, not as a record finding. Name searched at this commit: 0 archive directories and 0 `Row` elements in either registry layer match C-INDEX-METRIC.
C-INDEX-METRIC.Problem:
Three shipped facts, each re-read from `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts` at this commit and each first staged as F205. One: the index budget counts whole-file lines — `checkCeiling` feeds `newlineCount(xml)` to the index check at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1423`, and the retire path persists `persistSnapshot(indexPrev, newlineCount(indexXml), 40, true)` at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1244`. Two: retirement never removes an index line — `setEntryLayer` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:902`, called at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1197`) rewrites the `layer` attribute inside the existing open tag, so the `Entry` element stays in `decisions.xml` forever; the index is the one genre with no retired sibling. Three: the ceiling can only hold or fall — `persistSnapshot` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:942`) computes `min(previous.ceiling, ceilingBase + computedHeadroom)`, so the persisted 341 is a historical low-water mark. The consequence is measured: 256 live entries against a 341 ceiling with headroom 1 — one more entry and the record stops accepting findings at all, and no operation in the product can change that.
The breach diagnostic makes it worse than tight: `checkCeilingValue` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1498`) emits, for every genre, *"--retire / move the eligible entry to the retired sibling"* — a remedy that does not exist for the index genre. For the index, `--retire` moves nothing; the line stays. The message names an impossible operation and forbids the only other one.
Two shipped acceptance criteria stand behind parts of this behaviour and are overturned by this bundle, with their original arguments answered in the Goals. The charter fixes the remedy; this spec expresses it. Everything the traps probed — the split path's index metric, the two headroom sites, the golden fixture, the roots-invariant tripwire, the absence of any index-breach test, the prose that becomes false, and the module-anchor question — was answered from the tree, and each answer is in scope or explicitly out of it below.

Goals.Goal: V1 — the index budget is the live `Entry` count. The validator's index ceiling check and the retire path's index snapshot both measure direct `Entry` children of the `RecordIndex` root whose `layer` attribute is not `"retired"` — the mirror of `liveRowCount` (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:975`), which the registry budget already uses for rows. The unit change makes retirement relieve the index: when `--retire` flips an `Entry`'s layer in place, the live count falls, the next persist writes `base = live entries`, `headroom = constant`, `ceiling = min(previous, base + constant)`, and headroom is restored — measured on the C-RECORD-PARSE fixture with the converted engine in a throwaway tree: a `--retire` that flipped two entries wrote `base="272" headroom="40" ceiling="312"` where the shipped engine wrote the root line byte-identically (the ratchet, demonstrated on the fixture). The anti-raise property is unchanged: the clamp still only holds or falls, and no shipped operation raises the index ceiling.

M1 — the one-time root rewrite, in this bundle's own diff. The live `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml` root line is rewritten from `base="340" headroom="1" ceiling="341"` to the V1 unit — `base="256" headroom="40" ceiling="296"`, the values derived above — as a one-line attribute edit in this bundle's diff. No `Entry` is added, removed, or re-toned; no other record byte changes; findings, rulings and registry are untouched. The rewrite cannot be a `--retire` run: `retireRecord` early-returns before persisting any snapshot when nothing is eligible (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1134`), so the value is hand-written once — the same shape the rulings genre accepted when C-RETIRE-AND-CODIFY's one-time correction persisted its ceiling at commit `1896592`. That genre's answer to the hand-written value is the provenance guard (`RULINGS_PROVENANCE_CEILING`, declared at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:446`, compared inside `checkRulingsProvenance` at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1442`), and this bundle ships the matching guard for the index: a named exported constant holding the ceiling this diff persists, and a validation branch — a persisted index ceiling above the constant is an error whose message says no shipped operation raises it and says to restore from git, mirroring the rulings message. Without it, M1 leaves the index ceiling an unguarded hand-written value; with it, the guard's observation is exact and narrow: it fires only on a persisted index ceiling above the constant, so a hand edit raising a ceiling that the clamp has already pulled below the constant back up to — or anywhere under — the constant passes it clean. That residual window is stated here and accepted, not closed: the rulings guard carries the identical bound (the comparison inside `checkRulingsProvenance` at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:1442` fires only above `RULINGS_PROVENANCE_CEILING`), which is the precedent for accepting it, not a reason to overstate it. Falling stays legitimate — every value at or under the constant sits outside the guard's view by design.

The genre-aware breach diagnostic, shipped here. On an index ceiling breach the validator names an operation that exists: it reports the live-`Entry` count against the persisted ceiling, names `--retire` as the operation, and states the index mechanic — the eligible entries flip their index `Entry` layer to `"retired"` in place; the index has no retired sibling and its `Entry` lines stay. It keeps every prohibition the overturned criterion was protecting: it never names a config key or `ignoredDirs` as the remedy, and it keeps *"Raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy."* The other genres' message is unchanged. Measured with the converted engine on a fixture whose index ceiling was shrunk: the emitted `ceiling-exceeded` line reads *live index live-entry count 274 exceeds persisted ceiling 270; --retire / the eligible entries flip their index Entry layer to retired in place; the index has no retired sibling and its Entry lines stay. Raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy.*

The two overturns, answered rather than ignored. First — `AC-CEILINGS` in `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-RETIREMENT-2/spec.xml` (carried forward verbatim from `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-RECORD-RETIREMENT/spec.xml`): *"The failure message names the retirement operation (move the eligible entry to the retired sibling) and does not name a config key as the remedy."* This bundle overturns the parenthetical for the index genre only: the message still names the retirement operation and still never names a config key, and D28.1's ruling that the failure message names the retirement operation rather than the config key stands. The original argument — D28.1's *a budget that can be raised to pass is not a budget* — is answered by V1 itself, not around it: under the line metric the message's named operation could not return capacity, so the ceiling was the only enforcement and had to be unraisable; under the live-entry metric the named operation actually restores headroom (measured, first Goal), so the enforcement is the operation again and the ceiling returns to being the backstop D28.1 designed it to be. The raise path stays closed for every shipped operation — the clamp — and the provenance guard from the second Goal detects hand-raises above the constant, with its residual bound stated there. Second — `AC-ROOTS-CONSISTENT` in `.ngrace/changes/archive/C-PAYMENT-RECORD-4/spec.xml`: *"every persisted ceiling is byte-identical to its value at the base commit — ceilings are rewritten only by a move and never raised, so the post-payment roots must carry the ceiling attributes the pre-payment record carried."* This bundle overturns that criterion for the index genre: the ceiling falls 341 to 296 in this bundle's own diff. The original argument — ceilings must not drift silently — is answered by how loud the rewrite is: a ratified spec, this bundle's diff, and the derivation in the Summary, none of it silent; it is a fall, never a raise; and after it, the standing rule in `CLAUDE.md` (*"Ceiling attributes are rewritten only by the move and never raised"*) is true again for every operation that exists — the clamp persists, and the provenance guard detects any later hand-written raise above the constant, which is the same instrument the rulings genre got when its ceiling was written once, carrying the same bound: a raise from a fallen value back up to the constant sits inside the guard's blind spot, stated in the second Goal and in AC-INDEX-PROVENANCE-CEILING rather than implied closed.

The trap consequences, each decided from the tree. T1 — the split path: the one-time `--split` conversion computes its own index base and headroom (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:591`, `:595`, `:600`), today in lines. Measured on a minimal pre-split dump in a throwaway tree: the shipped engine writes `<RecordIndex base="4" headroom="40" ceiling="44">` for a two-entry index, and the converted validator accepts that output with exit 0 — so leaving `--split` on the old metric does not produce a rejection, it produces a silently wrong-unit snapshot that nothing shipped catches: the plain validator checks occupancy against the ceiling only, and the roots-invariant tripwire reads the real record, never split output. The split path's index base therefore moves to the live-`Entry` metric in this bundle — same expression as the retire path — so every writer of the index base is born in the right unit. T2 — the two headroom sites (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts:591` and `:1244`, both the literal 40, today in lines) become one named module-level constant denominated in entries, read by both sites, because T1 shows a wrong-unit snapshot validates clean and the constant removes the half-conversion class; the registry's duplicated literal 15 is the same shape with an unchanged unit, touching it is outside the charter, and this bundle leaves it alone. T3 — the golden fixture: the byte-for-byte golden test (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:1835`) pins seven files including `decisions.xml`, and the change invalidates exactly one of them — measured with the converted engine: the golden test fails on `decisions.xml` alone, and regenerating it and re-running the suite is green, the regenerated file differing from the committed one by exactly the root line, with both `f21` layer flips intact and `moved 3` unchanged. The regeneration of `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/decisions.xml` is in scope for this bundle. T4 — the roots-invariant tripwire (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2015`-2046) selects the shipped metric per file and reads the real record: its selection (`registry` gets live rows, everything else `newlineCount`, at `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2039`-2042) must learn the index rule, and because it reads the real record, the engine change, the test's metric change and the root rewrite must land in one commit — measured in the throwaway tree: the rewritten root against the old selection is red, the new selection against the rewritten root is green, and the suite is red in between either way. T5 — no existing test drives an index ceiling breach: both shipped `ceiling-exceeded` tests (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:183`-201 and `:634`-653) drive the breach through `findings`, and every index fixture the suite plants carries `ceiling="1000"`. The index-breach coverage in this bundle is therefore net-new, not an edit of an existing assertion. T6 and T7 are decided in the Constraints and NonGoals.

Constraints.Constraint: Ceremony tier T1 (module-change shape): the record-retirement engine, its suite, one fixture, one record root line, and governed prose. Roadmap: RM-GOVERNED-PATH (record integrity). Binding live rulings: D28 (every genre carries a retirement rule and a size ratchet — this bundle gives the index genre a retirement rule that works), D28.1 (the ceiling message names the retirement operation rather than the config key; ceilings are the backstop, eligibility-style rules the enforcement), D30 (a spec may not pin scalar counts of a file it changes into its hard Constraints — every number above is derivation or dated measurement context, and the Criteria below assert relations), D11 (no deferral without a dependency or conflict — the diagnostic ships here), D27 (nothing is approved unread; ratification is the maintainer's). Role split: the maintainer owns every outward-facing act; this bundle's executor authors artifacts from this spec and reports, and does not approve, commit, push, or run a gate.

Dynamic derivation, per D30. No hard Constraint in this spec transcribes a scalar count of any file it changes. The numbers 256, 40, 296, 272, 312, 338, 341 and 340 appear in this spec only as the derivation the charter required (R1) or as dated measurements in the Summary, Goals and Assumptions, each with the command or `file:line` it came from; every criterion asserts a relation its instrument can observe — base equals its shipped metric read back, base + headroom = ceiling — never a snapshot; the clamp relation (ceiling equals what the shipped `persistSnapshot` yields from the pre-rewrite persisted ceiling and the shipped headroom constant) is the derivation the rewritten values must carry, not an observation any standing instrument makes, and AC-INDEX-ROOT-REWRITTEN states which relations its instrument observes and which it does not. The values the rewritten root must carry are the ones this spec derives; if execution re-derives a disagreement, that disagreement is a finding for the authority, not a number to adopt silently.

Write scope, anchors — enumerated once (F136.1's rule). Files this spec forces into write scope: this bundle's own artifacts under `.ngrace/changes/active/C-INDEX-METRIC/`, and exactly six governed files — `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`; `scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts`; `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/decisions.xml` (byte regeneration only); `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml` (the root line only, the M1 rewrite); `CLAUDE.md`; `docs/plans/README.md`. `AGENTS.md` is in neither list because it is not a file: measured at this revision, `ls -la AGENTS.md` reports a symlink to `CLAUDE.md` (git mode 120000), so correcting `CLAUDE.md` corrects both names, and no plan task may write through the link — a write through it is either a no-op or replaces the link with a real file and silently un-twins the two names. Nothing under `src/` changes, and no record file other than the named root line changes. Anchor facts, re-checked at this revision: none of the six carries a `LINKS:` header, and no module in `.ngrace/graph/main.xml` declares any of them — the graph's modules own `src/**` paths plus M-SKILLS, and none of the six sits under an owned path. The record files carry no `LINKS:` header (the LINKS tokens inside them are prose in finding bodies and row Charters). AffectedAreas therefore names the single real anchor the C-RECORD-PARSE precedent used for this same file family — an anchor the gates accepted — and this spec does not mint a synthetic module, does not repeat this list as a second module list anywhere, does not register the record files in CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS, does not add a lint issue code, and does not change `.ngrace-lint.json`. Escape markup as character data (`<`, `>`, `&`) in every artifact this bundle writes; never paraphrase brackets away (F43's rule).

Evidence hygiene. Every criterion below is close-bound to a Command matching a shipped discriminating shape — read at `src/artifact/grammar.ts:100`-177 (`DEFAULT_CLOSE_EVIDENCE_COMMAND_SHAPES`) and `:191`-203 (`closeEvidenceCommandIsDiscriminating`, token-based over flattened text, so a shape match inside `bash -c` would also qualify): `bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts` (the bun-test shape) and `bun ./src/grace.ts lint --path . --fail-on warnings` (the grace.ts-lint shape). Each criterion's derivation names the mutation that would make its evidence red; where both directions exist, the criterion says what passes and what fails. No criterion compares a fixed `git show` against a floating working-tree read (E3): the one-time golden diff and the root rewrite are recorded as dated measurements in Assumptions, and the close-time instruments are the suite and the lint, which pin the end state without a base commit. Close-time lint runs at `--fail-on warnings`, so no CloseEvidence Command here may be undiscriminating. Findings raised while this bundle is open go to `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` under the next staged number the authority assigns, never into the record. The D30 freeze: this bundle's diff rewrites one root line and appends nothing; no dispatch that reads or rewrites the record is in flight with an append, and the authority performs the record write as part of this bundle's own approved diff.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Adding a tool mode, command, or flag for the rewrite or the metric. No new `--` mode on `scripts/validate-record-retirement.ts`, no second conversion pass, no interactive repair command. The rewrite is this bundle's own diff; the metric lives in the three existing call sites — the validator's index ceiling check, the retire path's index snapshot, and the split path's index base computation — so no new mode is needed to hold it. Owner: no one — chartered away by M1.

Giving the index a retired sibling, or re-deriving the ceiling from the current base. Both were considered and rejected by the charter, and this spec does not drift toward them: the index keeps every token, live and retired, because `layer` is the pointer to where the body lives; the ceiling keeps its clamp so no number can be raised to pass. Owner: no one — the charter's rejection is the position.

Changing any other genre's budget, message, or constant: the findings and rulings line budgets, the registry's live-row budget and its duplicated headroom literal, the rulings provenance guard, the eligibility findings, and `checkStatusFile` are untouched. Owner: unchanged surfaces — their units never changed, and no defect this bundle creates lives there.

Editing record bodies or the staged buffer: no prose inside `findings.xml`, `findings-retired.xml`, `registry-retired.xml` (which quote past messages and past charters as dated history), `rulings.xml`, `decisions.md`, `record-inventory.json`, or `.ngrace/scratch/staged-findings.md` is corrected by this bundle — the record's own process governs its bodies, and the buffer is the authority's. The M1 root-line rewrite is the only record byte in scope. Owner: the record's own process; the authority for the buffer.

Editing `README.md`, `examples/`, `skills/ngrace/`, `plugins/ngrace/skills/ngrace/`, `docs/plans/archive/`, `.ngrace/changes/archive/`, `package.json`, `bun.lock`, `.ngrace-lint.json`, or `CONTEXT_ARTIFACTS`, and any frozen test fixture under `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/` other than the one regenerated golden file (the fixture's `input/` snapshot, `parked-spec.xml`, `archive-names.json` and `baseline-probes.json` stay byte-identical). Owner: unchanged; no user-visible CLI token, config key, or ngrace command changes.

AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INDEX-METRIC-LIVE-ENTRIES:
The validator's index ceiling check and the retire path's index snapshot measure the live `Entry` count: direct `Entry` children of the `RecordIndex` root whose `layer` attribute is not `"retired"`. The suite gains the discriminating pair, net-new (T5): an index fixture whose whole-file line count exceeds its persisted ceiling while its live-`Entry` count does not must validate exit 0 — the exact fixture the shipped line metric fails; and an index fixture whose live-`Entry` count exceeds its persisted ceiling must exit non-zero with `ceiling-exceeded`. A fixture `--retire` that flips entries persists `base = live entries` and `headroom = constant` (the golden bytes pin the measured instance). Content question. Failure: either metric half reverted to `newlineCount` — the named mutation makes the green direction red; a ceiling raised to pass instead of the metric changed.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INDEX-BREACH-DIAGNOSTIC:
The index ceiling-breach message is genre-aware: it reports the live-`Entry` count against the persisted ceiling, names `--retire` as the operation, and states that the eligible entries flip their index `Entry` layer to `"retired"` in place, that the index has no retired sibling, and that the `Entry` lines stay; it keeps *"Raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy"*, and its flattened text contains neither `config key` nor `ignoredDirs`. The other genres' message is byte-unchanged. The suite gains the net-new test driving an index breach through a fixture with a shrunken index ceiling, asserting the message content on stderr, and asserting the findings-genre message still names the retired-sibling move. Content question. Failure: the shared remedy string restored for the index — the named mutation makes the new assertions red; a config-key remediation added — the prohibition assertions red.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-SPLIT-INDEX-METRIC:
The one-time `--split` conversion computes its index base in the live-`Entry` unit from the same named headroom constant the retire path reads (one module-level constant read at the two persist sites — T2's decision — inside the three call sites the metric conversion covers: the validator's index check, the retire persist, and this split base). The suite gains a net-new test that runs `--split` against a minimal pre-split dump in a throwaway root and asserts the written index root's relations: base equals the live-`Entry` count of the written index, headroom equals the shipped constant, ceiling equals base + headroom. Discriminates both ways (measured on the minimal dump): the shipped line-metric engine writes base = entries + 2 and fails this assertion; the converted engine passes. Failure: either call site reverting to a line computation or to a second literal — the split test or the golden bytes go red.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INDEX-PROVENANCE-CEILING:
The index gets the rulings genre's provenance guard: a named exported constant holding the ceiling this bundle's diff persists, and a validation branch that errors when a persisted index ceiling exceeds it — message mirroring the rulings provenance text: no shipped operation raises it, restore from git, raising the persisted ceiling is not the remedy. The suite gains the discriminating test, mirroring the T-003 provenance pair and stating its bound: an index ceiling at the provenance constant validates exit 0; one above it exits non-zero with the provenance message; and a ceiling the clamp has pulled below the constant, raised back up to it, validates exit 0 — the guard is silent there by design, and the test asserts that silence so the criterion states the instrument's exact bound instead of implying the window closed. The residual window is plain: the guard observes only ceilings above the constant, so a hand edit restoring a fallen ceiling to — or anywhere under — the constant is undetected; the rulings guard carries the identical bound, which is the precedent for accepting it, not a reason to overstate it. The constant's value is what the shipped `persistSnapshot` clamp yields from the pre-rewrite persisted ceiling and the shipped headroom constant — stated as that derivation in the code comment naming this bundle, never as a free-floating literal. Failure: the branch removed — the above-constant direction goes red; the comparison widened to fire at or under the constant — the at-constant and restore directions go red.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-ROOTS-TRIPWIRE-UNIT:
The production roots-invariant tripwire (`scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts:2015`-2046) selects the shipped metric per file with the index rule added: `registry` gets the live row count, `decisions.xml` gets the live-`Entry` count, findings and rulings keep `newlineCount`. The test reads the real record, so the engine change, this metric selection, and the M1 root rewrite must land in the same commit — measured in a throwaway tree, the suite is red in between in both partial orders. Content question. Failure: the selection reverted for `decisions.xml` against the rewritten root — the named mutation makes this test red while the rest of the suite stays green.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-INDEX-ROOT-REWRITTEN:
The live `docs/plans/active/RM-GOVERNED-PATH/decisions.xml` root carries the V1 unit as relations, not transcriptions, and this criterion claims only what its instrument observes: base equals its live-`Entry` count read back, and base + headroom = ceiling — the two assertions the roots-invariant test (the instrument the previous criterion wires) actually makes; re-read at this revision, that test compares neither `headroom` nor `ceiling` to any constant. The Summary's other two relations — headroom equals the shipped index headroom constant, ceiling equals the shipped `persistSnapshot` clamp applied to the pre-rewrite persisted ceiling — are therefore stated as derivation, not claimed as observation: no standing instrument can check the clamp relation without pinning the pre-rewrite persisted ceiling as a base-commit number, the floating-baseline defect the Evidence-hygiene Constraint forbids, and an instrument asserting `headroom` equals the constant would go red on the first legitimate append, which the clamp answers by holding the ceiling and shrinking headroom — under the constant is the clamp's own product, not drift. What stands over the unguarded direction is stated, not implied: the provenance branch of AC-INDEX-PROVENANCE-CEILING errors on a persisted ceiling above the constant, the golden bytes pin the measured fixture instance, and a hand-written root whose attributes hold any arithmetically consistent triple whose base equals the live count passes this criterion with its headroom under the constant — the residual window named rather than closed. No `Entry` element is added, removed, or re-toned by the rewrite, and no other record file changes. The plain validator exits 0 on the record. Content question, answered by parsing the root line. Failure: an observed relation broken — a mutated copy whose `base` disagrees with its live-`Entry` count, or whose three attributes are not internally consistent, turns the roots-invariant assertion red; an `Entry` count changed; a second record byte moved.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-GOLDEN-REGENERATED:
The golden test (`C-RECORD-PARSE golden`) is green against the converted engine: `scripts/fixtures/record-parse/golden/decisions.xml` is regenerated from the converted engine's fixture `--retire`, and the other six golden files are byte-identical to their committed state — measured before regeneration: with the converted engine the golden test fails on `decisions.xml` alone, and the regenerated file differs from the committed one by exactly the root attribute line (the dated diff is in Assumptions), which is why regeneration hides no behaviour change: the suite re-pins every other byte, both `f21` layer flips, and `moved 3`. Failure: any golden byte differing for a reason other than the root line — the diff recorded in Assumptions is the rule beside the number, and the golden test itself is the standing pin.
bun test scripts/validate-record-retirement.test.ts
AcceptanceCriteria.AC-GOVERNED-PROSE-CORRECTED:
The live governed prose states the index genre's actual retirement mechanic and does not present the retired-sibling move as the index remedy: `CLAUDE.md` and `docs/plans/README.md` — the only two live files carrying that prose, `AGENTS.md` being a symlink to `CLAUDE.md` with no bytes of its own and therefore neither edited nor written by any task — name that index `Entry` layers flip in place and that the index has no retired sibling — minimal edits that keep every token the suite's existing CLAUDE/README teaching test requires (`decisions.md`, `decisions.xml`, `findings`, `decisions`, `registry`, `index`, `live`, `retired`, `--retire`, `re-derives PaidBy`, `never raised`, `resolving CodifiedIn`, *a resolving TaughtIn does not move it*), which this bundle extends to require the index-flip clause so the prose cannot silently regress. Frozen surfaces are named in NonGoals and are not edited. Content question. Failure: the clause removed from either named file — the extended test goes red. A twin-divergence failure mode is deliberately absent: it cannot occur, one file carrying two names, and a criterion whose evidence cannot go red is a defect, not a formality.

Post-archive lint 0/0. This is the only place current-mode lint of this root appears.

C-INDEX-METRIC.AffectedAreas: The one graph anchor above is kept, and its justification is the rule itself, re-derived at this revision rather than borrowed from precedent — the precedent argument does not transfer, because both cited bundles wrote files under `src/artifact/`, which this bundle never does. The governing rule, read at `validateGraphAnchorsOwnWriteScope` (`src/lint/core.ts:740`) with its predicate `isModuleOwnableWritePath` (`src/lint/core.ts:724`): the error `change.graph-anchors-miss-write-scope` (raised at `src/lint/core.ts:766`) can fire only when an active plan's ObservedWriteScope names a path under `src/` that is not a test file and whose own MODULE_CONTRACT `LINKS` modules include no module in the plan's GraphAnchors.
